headline: WHICH GLASSES
ARE **FILMING**?
cover.hook_pick_reason: Slide 2 shows officials could not tell which glasses were filming, and slide 3 shows why (a cheap sticker over the recording light). It asks the reader the same question. The sticker option is backed but the dollar figure is a conversion, so the won figure stays inside.
cover.image_prompt: Cinematic close-up of a pair of plain black eyeglasses with a thick frame resting on a dark wooden desk, a tiny lens on the hinge and a small dark square sticker covering a tiny indicator light, soft amber rim light, cool blue background haze. No text, no letters, no logos, no people, no faces.

slides.title: Spot the camera
body: At Korea's parliamentary audit on Oct. 23, lawmaker **Lee Jung-hun** of the ruling Democratic Party had aides wear ordinary glasses and AI smart glasses. Officials could not tell which pair was filming.

slides.title: A sticker beats the light
body: Smart glasses show an LED when they record. Blocking stickers sold online for about **2,000 won** (under $2) cover it.

slides.title: It is already happening
body: Lee's office found **three cases** this year of people caught filming illegally with smart glasses, including filming a flight attendant and filming in a hotel. Police keep no official statistics.

slides.title: Rules lag behind
body: A ministry policy study won't report until **summer 2027**, police have no enforcement manual and the privacy watchdog's powers are limited. Lee said the glasses are reaching exams like TOEIC, and pointed to curbs in Australia.

slides.title: A cross-ministry plan
body: Bae Kyung-hoon, Korea's deputy prime minister and science minister, said the issue came up at a cabinet meeting and promised a **cross-ministry** response and faster work on guidelines.

facts.text: Oct. 23 audit of the National Assembly science and ICT committee; Democratic Party lawmaker Lee Jung-hun had aides wear ordinary glasses and AI glasses; officials could not tell which was filming.
The recording LED was covered with a blocking sticker sold online for about 2,000 won. Dollar figure is our approximation (2,000 won is under $2 at any recent rate), not from the article.
Three cases this year of illegal filming with smart glasses caught, including a flight attendant and a hotel; no official police statistics.
Policy study results not until summer 2027; no police manual; Personal Information Protection Commission has limited authority; Australia restricts smart glasses.
Deputy Prime Minister and Science Minister Bae Kyung-hoon said it was discussed at the cabinet meeting and promised a cross-ministry response and faster guidelines.
Lee said smart glasses are entering national qualification exams, TOEIC, universities and essay tests, and the government response is almost nonexistent.

caption:
Korea's lawmakers showed that AI smart glasses can film people without anyone noticing, even officials who were looking for it.

At a parliamentary audit, a cheap sticker over the recording light was enough to hide which glasses were filming.

→ Blocking stickers sell online for about 2,000 won (under $2)
→ Three smart-glasses filming cases were caught this year
→ Korea's science minister promised a cross-ministry plan

Would you notice if the person next to you was recording?

Source: ZDNet Korea, "AI glasses as hidden cameras demonstrated at audit; Bae Kyung-hoon: \"We will prepare cross-ministry measures\"" (in Korean), Oct 23, 2026; Money Today, "Smart-glasses recording light 'defeated for 2,000 won'; ruling party's Lee Jung-hun: \"Measures are needed\"" (in Korean), Oct 23, 2026.
